en.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
en.author: Phillips Brooks
stanzas:
[G]O little town of [E7]Bethlehem,
how [Am]still we [D7]see thee [G]lie!
A[G]bove thy deep and [E7]dreamless sleep
the [Am]silent [D7]stars go [G]by.
Yet [Em]in thy [B7]dark streets [Em]shineth
the [Am]ever[B7]lasting [Em]light;
the [G]hopes and fears of [E7]all the years
are [Am]met in [D7]thee to[G]night.

For Christ is born of Mary;
and, gathered all above,
while mortals sleep, the angels keep
their watch of wond'ring love.
O morning stars, together
proclaim the holy birth,
and praises sing to God the King,
and peace to men on earth.

How silently, how silently,
the wondrous gift is giv'n!
So God imparts to human hearts
the blessings of His heav'n.
No ear may hear His coming,
but in this world of sin,
where meek souls will receive Him still,
the dear Christ enters in.

notes: Text: hymnary.org representative text (from Psalms and Hymns to the Living God #232), the standard four-stanza selection; Brooks's original fifth stanza ('Where children pure and happy') is rarely printed and omitted. Tune ST. LOUIS (Redner); meter 8.6.8.6 D as the hymnary text page lists it (lines 5-6 are actually 7.6). Hymnary gives the tune's key as 'F Major/G Major or modal'; G is itself a listed common key, so no transposition. Chart is the common simplified guitar harmonization (the E7-Am move standing in for Redner's chromatic passing harmony); middle couplet charted in the relative minor per the tune.
